analysis.title: UBS House View Monthly Letter: Divided (22 October 2026)
key_insights: UBS estimates a 90% chance the November US midterms produce divided government, with Democrats controlling at least one chamber. It says earnings, AI and rates should matter more for portfolios than the election, and it would not treat the midterms as a binary directional market event.

UBS forecasts Q3 S&P 500 EPS growth of 28% y/y (the Investment ideas section cites a 25-30% range). Semiconductor profits contribute about half of that growth. Drivers are AI demand, an improving industrial cycle and resilient higher-income consumers.

UBS expects AI capital spending of USD 900bn this year and average cloud revenue growth to accelerate from 48% in the June quarter to 58% y/y in the September quarter. Management commentary on pricing, capacity constraints and returns on investment will shape expectations.

Risks are rising in the more capital-intensive parts of the AI buildout, where funding pressure and execution risk could reinforce each other. Recent share-price pressure on neoclouds (specialized compute-rental providers) illustrates this. UBS still sees broad demand as robust, citing rising GPU rental prices and strong semiconductor earnings.

UBS limits exposure to neoclouds and favors well-funded hyperscalers for better risk-reward. It also likes high-quality semiconductor and hardware beneficiaries of AI spending. It suggests considering defensive tech areas such as payment networks, select consumer electronics and select software.

Cyclical earnings look supported. The ISM Manufacturing new orders component has been in expansion for nine consecutive months, and US retail sales grew 6% y/y in September despite pressure on lower-income households from energy costs and rates. Non-financial S&P 500 companies have a weighted average debt maturity of about 11 years.

UBS forecasts 15% Eurozone earnings growth in both 2026 and 2027, helped by manufacturing, cost discipline and investment in AI, electrification and defense. French political risk may cause volatility. In the last ten Fed tightening periods, European equities averaged +5% after six months and +14% after 12 months.

UBS rates Asian equities Attractive and expects 20% profit growth next year. MSCI Asia ex-Japan trades at about 9x 12-month forward P/E, a multi-decade low, and earnings growth has run well ahead of price gains this year.

UBS expects the S&P 500 to reach 8,400 by end-June 2027. It likes AI, power and resources, and longevity themes. In the US it likes financials, industrials, utilities, health care and consumer discretionary. It also likes Eurozone equities, plus Japan, India, Taiwan and Singapore.

The US 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.36% in early October, its highest since 2002, and has eased to about 5.1%. The German 10-year Bund yield rose above 3.6% in late September, and the French 10-year yield was above 5%.

US monthly CPI accelerated to 0.6% in September from 0.4% in August, with core at 0.3% for a second month. Eurozone headline inflation reached a three-year high of 3.8% y/y. UBS now expects the Fed to raise rates again in both December and March because policymakers worry about de-anchored inflation expectations.

Futures price roughly three more Fed hikes, slightly more than UBS expects. UBS's base case is a moderate decline in yields over 12 months and it rates fixed income Attractive. It favors medium- and longer-duration high-quality bonds and stays cautious on the longest maturities because of fiscal concerns and heavy issuance, including AI-related fundraising.

Breakeven yield rises (the increase needed for capital losses to offset one year of income) are about 254bp for 2-year, 113bp for 5-year and 65bp for 10-year Treasuries. UBS calls such moves unlikely because policymakers would likely respond.

The French-German 10-year spread has widened about 75bp over three months to 158bp, which UBS reads as a premium for fiscal concerns. Contagion has widened other Eurozone sovereign spreads and weighed on the euro.

Middle East crude and product exports were about 80% of pre-conflict levels in September, helped by partial Strait of Hormuz flows (including dark shipping) and pipeline rerouting. UKMTO counted 26 confirmed Iranian attacks on Hormuz shipping from 1 to 18 October, against 14 for all of September. Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries resumed, and the Saudi-Houthi conflict still threatens energy infrastructure.

Brent has risen from a June low of USD 72/bbl to about USD 110/bbl. UBS's base case is that it stays high near term and moderates to USD 90/bbl in 1H27 as pipeline flows and non-Middle East supply grow. A diplomatic deal that normalizes flows would likely bring prices down faster. Shipping from the Middle East to Asia costs USD 30-40/bbl against under USD 5/bbl before the conflict.

Oil is about USD 40/bbl higher on average than last year. UBS estimates that could cut global GDP growth by 0.3-0.5 points in isolation, but AI investment and household balance sheets have kept consumption resilient. OPEC crude output rose 0.92 mb/d m/m in September to 25.1 mb/d.

Refined products are disconnected from crude. Global refinery throughput was 81.8 mb/d in September, about 2.8 mb/d below a year earlier, per the IEA. UBS models a risk scenario with US gasoline at USD 170/bbl and wholesale diesel at USD 250/bbl (from about USD 130 and USD 200). That would slow US growth toward the low 1% range, not cause a recession.

UBS says geopolitics alone does not justify a defensive stance. It recommends broad commodity exposure, including energy, for diversification and protection against prolonged supply disruption, to be actively managed and sized for volatility. It says tight physical markets support a commodity upcycle.

UBS gives 50% to a Democratic sweep, 40% to split control and 10% to Republicans keeping both chambers in the 3 November midterms. Narrow majorities and the presidential veto limit sweeping legislation, and the president keeps authority over tariffs, foreign policy and regulation. A change of control is not expected to derail data center expansion, and reversing the enacted tax cuts is unlikely. Debt ceiling talks in 2027 could create volatility.

UBS suggests capital preservation strategies for investors with concentrated positions, large gains, lower loss tolerance or near-term liquidity needs. It also recommends putting excess cash to work in phases, investing in AI, power and resources, and longevity themes, and diversifying with alternatives.

sector_views.sector: US financials, industrials, utilities, health care, consumer discretionary
sector_views.rationale: Named as preferred US sectors within a diversified mix of cyclical and structural growth.
The Transformational Innovation themes and the preferred structural exposures.
Funding and construction pressures. UBS limits exposure and prefers well-funded hyperscalers.
Tight physical markets, a commodity upcycle and diversification against supply disruption.
Yields offer sufficient income to cushion further rises. UBS stays cautious on the longest maturities.
Expected 15% Eurozone EPS growth in 2026 and 2027. Asian valuations at multi-decade lows with 20% profit growth expected next year.

earnings_insights: UBS forecasts Q3 2026 S&P 500 EPS growth of 28% y/y (UBS CIO estimate, not yet reported), with semiconductors contributing about half. The Investment ideas section cites 25-30%.
UBS forecasts average cloud revenue growth of 58% y/y in the September quarter (UBS estimate), up from 48% in the June quarter.
UBS forecasts 15% Eurozone earnings growth in both 2026 and 2027, and 20% profit growth in Asia next year (UBS estimates).

trade_ideas.description: Hold diversified equity exposure across cyclical and structural growth (AI, power and resources, longevity), and trim concentrated single-stock positions.
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong earnings growth should support the equity rally, while higher rates and energy costs call for selectivity.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher rates, energy costs, geopolitical risks and uncertainty over AI monetization.

trade_ideas.rationale: Yields give enough income to cushion further rises, and bonds hedge growth downside.

risk_factors: Further rise in bond yields and persistent inflation, with Fed tightening.
Fiscal concerns and elevated issuance, including AI-related fundraising.
French fiscal and political risk, and contagion across Eurozone spreads and the euro.
A prolonged oil and diesel supply shock from Hormuz attacks and attacks on Russian and Middle East energy infrastructure.
Funding and execution pressure in capital-intensive AI areas such as neoclouds.
AI monetization uncertainty and the exceptional pace of AI investment.
Pressure on lower-income households from higher energy costs and interest rates.
charts_described: Figure 1: Contribution to S&P 500 EPS y/y growth from semis and non-semis, actuals and CIO estimates through 4Q26E, plus bond spreads for IG hyperscalers, the IG corporate index and HY data centers.
Figure 2: Rise in US Treasury yields needed for capital losses to offset one year of income: 254bp for 2-year, 113bp for 5-year, 65bp for 10-year.
Figure 3: US crude (WTI), gasoline and diesel prices from 2021 to 2026, showing refined products have risen further than crude.
Figure 4: CIO EPS growth forecasts for 2026 and 2027 by region (EMU, US, AC World, UK, Switzerland, Japan, EM, China, AxJ).
vol_and_positioning: UBS suggests capital preservation strategies to limit drawdowns while staying invested, especially for concentrated positions and investors with large gains.
UBS recommends using market strength to reduce concentrated single-stock positions.
Fed funds futures price roughly three further hikes, slightly more than UBS expects.
geopolitical: Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz: 26 confirmed attacks from 1 to 18 October against 14 in all of September (UKMTO).
Russia continues striking Ukraine, and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries and oil infrastructure resumed after a brief halt.
The Saudi Arabia-Houthi conflict continues to pose a risk to energy infrastructure.
US midterm elections on 3 November: 50% Democratic sweep, 40% split control, 10% Republicans hold both chambers.
French political and fiscal risk: the OAT-Bund spread has widened to 158bp.
Middle East wars and the Ukraine war are adding to inflation.

tension_points.bull_case: Q3 S&P 500 EPS is forecast to grow 28% y/y, cloud revenue growth to accelerate to 58%, and GPU rental prices and semiconductor earnings are rising.
tension_points.bear_case: Capital-intensive AI areas face funding and execution pressure, as share-price weakness in neoclouds shows, and semiconductors are about half of earnings growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Management commentary on AI adoption and monetization that shows the pace of AI investment cannot continue.

tension_points.bull_case: Easing inflation should pull yields lower over 12 months, and current yields cover a further rise (breakevens of 254/113/65bp).
tension_points.bear_case: Renewed inflation, further Fed hikes (December and March expected), fiscal concerns and heavy issuance could push yields higher.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A yield spike larger than the breakeven moves (about 65bp on the 10-year over a year) would offset income with capital losses.

tension_points.bull_case: Flows are partly restored, pipelines are adapting, and Brent is expected to moderate to USD 90/bbl in 1H27. Growth impact has been limited.
tension_points.bear_case: Attacks on shipping and refineries are rising, and refined-product prices could reach USD 170 gasoline and USD 250 diesel, slowing US growth toward the low 1% range.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A significant and sustained rise in oil prices from current levels.
